evidence.claim: The server sends a 304 Not Modified response when the ETag matches the current resource.
evidence.quote: Because the etag value matches at the time of the request, the entity tag fails the condition, and a 304 response is returned:
evidence.title: 304 Not Modified
sub_questions: What response does the server send when the ETag matches the current resource?
evidence.support_reason: The quote states that when the etag value matches, a 304 response is returned.

evidence.claim: The client reuses its cached representation and does not download the response body when receiving a 304 Not Modified.
evidence.quote: The response carries no message body and instructs the client to reuse its stored representation.
evidence.title: 304 Not Modified
sub_questions: How does the client interpret a 304 Not Modified response to avoid downloading the body?
evidence.support_reason: The quote states the response has no message body and instructs reuse of the stored representation, matching the claim that the client does not download a body and reuses the cache.

evidence.claim: When a 304 Not Modified is returned, the response must include Cache‑Control, Content‑Location, Date, ETag, Expires, and Vary headers.
evidence.quote: When the server returns 304, the response includes headers from the original successful response: Cache-Control, Content-Location, Date, ETag, Expires, and Vary.
evidence.title: If-None-Match
sub_questions: Are there any caveats or additional headers involved in this caching mechanism?
evidence.support_reason: The quote lists the same headers and states they are included in a 304 response, matching the claim.

evidence.claim: When the condition fails for GET and HEAD methods, the server must return a 304 Not Modified and any of the following header fields that would have been sent in a 200 response to the same request: Cache‑Control, Content‑Location, Date, ETag, Expires, and Vary.
evidence.quote: When the condition fails for GET and HEAD methods, the server must return a 304 Not Modified and any of the following header fields that would have been sent in a 200 response to the same request: Cache-Control, Content-Location, Date, ETag, Expires, and Vary.
evidence.title: If-None-Match header
sub_questions: Are there any caveats or additional headers involved in this caching mechanism?
evidence.support_reason: The quote states exactly the same conditions and header fields as the claim.
